newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Micro shares rise on new chip.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Micro shares rise on new chip.

text.p: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc rose 3-7/8 to 45-5/8 by mid-afternoon Wednesday behind positive comments by one analyst and heightened feelings its new K6 microchip will be welcomed by computer makers.
"The increasing sense is that the K6 is for real and will be coming out in the second quarter," said Dan Klesken, analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co.

He also said a recently signed deal by Cyrix Corp to make microprocessors for Compaq Computer Corp has led industry watchers to think computer makers are now willing to use chips made by rivals of giant Intel Corp.
"Compaq's move shows us the customers, PC OEMs (original equipment manufacturers), have a little more open mind to work with the Cyrixes and AMDs of the world," Klesken said.
The K6 chip is Advanced Micro Devices' competing product to Intel's high-end Pentium microprocessors and its new Pentium II chip set to be launched in the second quarter.

An Advanced Micro spokesman noted the K6's launch, also set for the second quarter, marks the first time Advanced Micro has launched a direct competitor to an Intel chip in the same time frame as Intel.
Recent reviews in two German magazines said the Pentium II's performance paled in comparison to the K6, according to a report in today's New York Times.

Also, Prudential Securities analyst Mark Edelstone reiterated a buy rating on Advanced Micro's stock and raised his 12-month price target to $90 a share from $40. He based the new target on a 1998 earnings estimate of $5.25 a share.
